I have been keeping this note for a few months now as a simple way to track the bigger choices I make. Life feels like it moves fast sometimes, and I forget why I picked one path over another. Having a dated log helps me look back without second-guessing everything. I usually sit down with a cup of coffee on Sunday mornings, review the past week, and add anything important. The house is quiet then, just the sound of the neighbor's dog barking occasionally and the heater clicking on and off.

Most of these decisions are small in the grand scheme, but they shape my daily routine and long-term plans. I try to write a short explanation for each one so future me understands the context. I also link to related notes like [[class-schedule]] or [[phd-applications]] when it makes sense.

### 2026-01-12 - Dropping Spanish Class
Tuesday evenings had become exhausting. Between the commute to campus, the actual class, and then trying to practice conversation exercises at home, I was burning out. I really enjoyed learning the language at first, especially the food-related vocabulary, but it was starting to cut into my research time. After talking it over with Sarah during one of our long walks, I decided to drop the Spanish class to free up Tuesday evenings. It feels like the right call. Now I can use that time for reading papers or just relaxing with a book. I still plan to practice Duolingo a few times a week so I don't lose everything I learned. [[language-learning]] has more notes on this.

### 2026-02-02 - Choosing Zotero over Mendeley
Citation management has been a headache for the last year. I kept switching between different tools and wasting time formatting references manually. After spending an entire afternoon comparing features, watching tutorials, and asking in the [[grad-student-discord]], I decided to use Zotero over Mendeley for citations. The browser connector works better for me, and the local storage option gives me more control over my data. Mendeley felt too tied to Elsevier. I spent the following weekend migrating my old library and setting up shared collections with my lab mates. So far it has been smooth. I still need to explore the PDF annotation features more.

### 2026-02-20 - Limiting PhD Applications
Applying to graduate programs is stressful and expensive. I realized I was spreading myself too thin by considering eight or nine schools. After reviewing program rankings, talking with my advisor, and making a big spreadsheet of funding opportunities, I decided to apply to only 3 PhD programs (CMU, Michigan, UW). These three feel like the best fit for my interest in human-computer interaction and have strong funding records. Writing fewer tailored statements means I can make them actually good instead of generic. I finished the CMU one last night and it felt solid. The deadlines are coming up fast, so I need to stay focused. See [[phd-application-tracker]] for details on each school.

### 2026-03-01 - Stopping Notion Usage
I have been a heavy Notion user for almost two years. At first it was great for organizing everything in one place, but lately the pages feel cluttered and the mobile experience is slow. After a long discussion in the [[productivity-chat]] group and testing a few alternatives, I decided to stop using Notion. I am moving most of my daily notes and project tracking into Obsidian. The local files and [[wikilinks]] feel more reliable for long-term thinking. It took me three evenings to export and reorganize everything, but I already notice I am writing more freely. I still use Notion for a couple of shared team dashboards at work, but my personal knowledge base is now fully here. This change also pairs nicely with the switch to Zotero since both tools integrate well with markdown.

These four choices have freed up mental space more than I expected. I feel lighter, like I am no longer carrying decisions that no longer serve me. I will keep adding to this log as new ones come up. Next on my mind is whether to commit to the summer internship at the tech company or focus on finishing my thesis draft. Maybe I will write that one up next weekend.
